newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Long bonds were dealt a severe dose of whiplash on Friday as a rash of negative factors propelled the market 20-basis points weaker.
At 1400 GMT, the key R150 was pegged at a 14.86 percent yield from 14.66 percent overnight after trading as high as 14.89 percent during the day.
The market started off the day under pressure from institutional selling after the yield on the U.S. benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose to 7.13 percent from 7.08 percent in New York overnight.

By 0730, the R150 had reached 14.76 percent as jobbers took up the cudgels when Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals, in a speech at a conference in Durban, warned that recent growth in money supply and bank credit extension begged the question whether interest rates needed to rise.

"Recent trends in the money supply and bank credit extension beg the question...whether even more stringent measures may not be required to reduce overall liquidity further, which could, of course, lead to even higher interest rates...," Stals said.
The comments spooked the market, prompting both jobbers and foreigners to jettison stock and catapult yields 12 basis points higher within the next 40 minutes.
By early afternoon, the market had settled as buyers surfaced and brought the market back down to around the 14.82 percent level.
Buyers were given a further fillip when the Customs and Excise department announced that South Africa's trade balance swung 2.5 billion rand into the black in March to a 1.98 billion rand surplus.

The kneejerk reaction to 14.79 was short-lived, however, and the market spent the rest of the afternoon session drifting higher as players positioned themselves for the release of March money supply and credit extension data at 1500 GMT.
Dealers said Stals' comments had taken the edge off economists' expectations that burgeoning credit demand had finally started to slow in the month.
Market consensus called for a 16.50 percent increase from a preliminary 17.34 percent in February.
"Stals comments were not really appreciated by the market," one senior trader said. "Everyone is nervous about the figures."
Dealers said that direction in the week ahead, which will be shortened by public holidays on Monday and Thursday, would be determined by the data.
If the figure was unchanged or negative, yields could head back up to the 15.00 percent level, while a positive number could see yields retrace back to around the 14.70 level.
Dealers noted that various technical resistance lines had formed between 14.65 and 14.70 percent and that the market would find it difficult to break below those levels in the short-term.
On the currency market, the rand treaded water for much of the day before local position squaring later in the day ahead of the data pushed the rand over the 4.45 level.
At 1400 GMT it was pegged at 4.4500/4530 against the dollar from 4.4420/4450 overnight.
The rand had traded in a tight 4.4400 bid to 4.4450 bid range for much of the day before a local order to buy dollars livened up trade from about 1500 GMT onwards.

"We saw some interest to buy dollars from the local banks late in the afternoon," a trader said. "The market is a bit nervous about being short going into this figure," she said, adding that players had also squared up their positions ahead of the long-weekend.
Direction next week would be determined by the credit and M3 data, dealers said.
If the number was positive, they said the currency could break below the 4.44 level in the week ahead. If negative, the rand could move up to 4.46.
At either end, though, dealers said there was both good importer interest to buy dollars at 4.44 and exporter and foreign interest to sell around 4.46.

Against the crosses, the rand was last trading at 28.1994/2408 yen from 28.3568/3872 yen on Thursday, at 0.3856/3860 marks compared with 0.3865/3870 marks previously and at 7.2329/2422 against sterling from 7.2227/2307 before.
Major banks kept their three month deposit rates steady at between 16.40 to 16.45 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at between 15.80 to 15.95 percent.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage rose to 7.621 billion rand on Thursday from 7.372 billion rand on Wednesday.
